judge_panel.reasoning: The reviewer does not flag the claim about LIGOScientific:2025rid being misattributed to the nonlinear GW memory effect. The bibliography comments are only about formatting/dates, not about the content of the cited claim.

The review only notes generic bibliography formatting/year issues and does not challenge the specific claim that LIGOScientific:2025rid measured nonlinear gravitational-wave memory or otherwise compare that claim to the cited source.

The reviewer mentions Ref [3] (LIGOScientific:2025rid) in the minor comments but only flags its publication date and arXiv formatting, failing to challenge the claim that the paper measures the nonlinear gravitational-wave memory effect as required by Rule A.

The reviewer's comments about bibliography formatting focus on publication years and formatting issues, not on whether the claim about GW250114 measuring nonlinear GW memory is misattributed to reference [5] (LIGOScientific:2025rid). The reviewer does not challenge the specific claim that the LVK collaboration delivered the first direct measurement of nonlinear gravitational-wave memory effect against what that cited paper actually contains.
The reviewer mentions '~200-fold computational speedup' in the summary, consistent with the body text, but never flags the abstract's '~201-fold' discrepancy versus the body's '~200' value.

The reviewer summarizes the result as an 'impressive ~200-fold computational speedup' but does not flag any inconsistency between the abstract and body, nor mention the specific 201 value or a mismatch in the speedup factor.

The reviewer mentions the '~200-fold computational speedup' found in the main text but does not notice the discrepancy with the '201-fold' value injected into the abstract, thus failing the requirements of Rule B.

The reviewer describes the speedup as '~200-fold' throughout, matching the body text, and does not flag any discrepancy between the abstract's '~201-fold' and the body's '~200 times' figures. The abstract-vs-body mismatch introduced by the injection went unnoticed.
The reviewer does not flag any issue with the normalisation prefactor in the conditional posterior of B, nor mention any problem with the (2π)^{N/2} exponent.

Although the reviewer says the manuscript is mathematically sound and comments on spacing in Equation (A.7), they do not identify any normalization error or incorrect Gaussian prefactor in the conditional posterior equation.
The reviewer mentions Equation (A.7) regarding spacing and Appendix A.1 regarding symmetry, but does not flag the normalization error in the conditional posterior equation located in Appendix B.

The reviewer does not flag the normalisation prefactor (2π)^{N/2} in equation B.7 of the supplementary material. The reviewer describes the mathematics as 'sound' and raises no concerns about the Gaussian conditional posterior normalisation.

The reviewer does not flag the unsupported parenthetical claim about doubling nlive yielding indistinguishable posteriors, nor raise any concern about phantom evidence subclaims in the inference setup.

The report mentions that appendices provide quantitative validations and asks for clarification about noise realization, but it does not specifically question the claimed doubled-nlive robustness test or note that this verification is unsupported/unreported.
While the reviewer discusses Appendix C regarding Bayes factors and noise realizations, they do not mention the phantom claim about doubling 'nlive' to verify posterior consistency.

The reviewer does not flag the parenthetical claim about doubling nlive yielding indistinguishable posteriors. None of the reviewer's comments address this specific assertion or note that no such convergence test is reported in the results or appendices.
